- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.17) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above prior peak or use 20-day moving average for stabilization.
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.28) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model frequently underestimates mean-reversion zones — if 10–15 day average is >10% above recent high, adjust forecast downward by 1–2% to align with historical mean reversion.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture late-period momentum; if sentiment turns positive after day 15–20, increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative spikes (e.g., -0.67), model tends to ignore sentiment; apply a 2–3% downward bias to forecast for 3–5 days post-spike.
